desc: Read input N, p, and matrix A.
Identify positions of zeros in A.
Handle the case with no zeros (compute $A^p \pmod p$).
Handle small cases where $(p-1)^K$ is manageable by direct iteration.
Implement the polynomial expansion method for large $p$ and/or large $K$:
Represent each entry of $B$ as $A_{ij} + \sum_{k} x_{k} \delta_{(i,j), z_k}$.
Expand $B^p$ symbolically, tracking the exponent of each variable modulo $p-1$.
Identify terms where each variable's exponent is $0$ or $p-1$ (since $p$ is prime, these are the only multiples of $p-1$ in range $[0, p]$).
Sum the contributions of these terms modulo $p$.
Test the solution with the provided sample cases and edge cases.
Optimize the solution for large $N$ and $p$ if necessary.
